derivation.max_transition_logical_note: 48 MiB: state checkpoint + event checkpoint + event proof, each 16 MiB
derivation.subsequent_note: the state rewrite reuses pages freed in the same transaction; only the event row grows
derivation.owner_cap_rationale: Target: admit three consecutive maximum-size transitions (a non-terminal one, then a terminal one, then one more). Smallest power-of-two page count meeting that target is 32768; 16384 admits only one further maximum-size transition. Measured fill: 8 -> 12308 -> 20508 -> 28708 pages; the fourth would reach 36908 and is refused with SQLITE_FULL. The 3-transition target is a judgment, not derived from workflow budgets. This caps storage; it is not a promise that unlimited workflow history fits.
derivation.root_cap_rationale: Root rows hold digests, timestamps, paths, and incarnation JSON capped at 4096 bytes by schema CHECK. 4096 pages (16 MiB) is a conservative storage bound for the host-only namespace. Root growth was NOT measured end to end in this increment.

enforcement: Every writable owner and protected-root connection is opened with _auto_vacuum=NONE, page_size=4096, and max_page_count=<cap> in the DSN. max_page_count is per connection and is not persisted: a plain connection reports SQLite default 4294967294 (measured), so the DSN is the enforcement point and pooled replacements re-apply it.
Fresh create verifies geometry before journal_mode=WAL (which writes page 1) and before schema DDL.

Existing writable open verifies geometry before any other statement and refuses page_size != 4096, auto_vacuum != 0, page_count > cap (explicit check, because SQLite raises a ceiling below the current size up to that size), and read-back max_page_count != cap. Geometry refusals return ErrOwnerStore. Byte-identity (SHA-256 equality) was tested only for files without a retained WAL; a writable close checkpoints and deletes a retained WAL, so it is not established for that case. Corrected in sqlite-geometry-preflight-20261015.json: a read-only geometry precheck now runs before the writable open.
Read-only historical seam (openSettledOwnerDatabase / LoadSettledCheckpoint) is unchanged: no limit-setting PRAGMA and no geometry refusal added there.
No VACUUM, no auto-vacuum enablement, and no migration in product code. VACUUM appears only in test fixtures that create incompatible files.

SQLITE_FULL at statement time (for example INSERT) rolls back and reaches callers as errors.Join(ErrCAS, ErrOwnerStore) wrapping modernc *sqlite.Error code 13; no receipt or effect binding is returned and the owner is not poisoned. Commit-time failures keep the existing poisoning behavior.

open_assumptions: WAL is not bounded by the page ceiling. A reader holding a snapshot (for example a concurrent process on the read-only seam) can block WAL reset and let WAL grow across transactions. Retained WAL currently equals the largest single transaction (50.8 MB measured).

The ceiling is storage-only. After three maximum-size transitions further growth is refused with SQLITE_FULL; this does not guarantee that terminal settlement fits. Terminal headroom must be reserved before a new effect (next increment).
Host backing storage, dedicated filesystem or quota identity, and filesystem allocation/journal overhead are not established.
Pre-existing files created at base commit use SQLite default page size 4096 and auto_vacuum NONE (inferred from the engine default; not checked against a base-commit artifact).
Root cap derivation is from schema row limits; per-workflow root growth is not measured.
Only the pinned engine (SQLite 3.53.4 via modernc.org/sqlite v1.60.1) was exercised.
